copies.headline: Adam's Receivers Buried Noah's Wilsons
copies.body:
The wideouts decided this one. Adam got 39.7 from Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Chris Olave; Noah got 15.6 from Garrett Wilson and Michael Wilson, a 24.1-point hole that happens to be the exact final margin. Everything else was noise. Noah actually won the game at quarterback and tight end — Drake Maye's 23.8 and Colston Loveland's 18.5 against Mark Andrews turning in 1.4 — and still never led in any meaningful way, because when your two starting receivers combine for less than Adam's kicker and flex, the math stops being negotiable.
Noah's misses compound. Rhamondre Stevenson managed 3.6 on a 13.3 projection, and Hunter Henry put up 14.8 on the bench while Josh Downs started for 8.7. Six points of Browns D/ST also rotted there. Adam, meanwhile, posted his season low at 132.7 and won by 24.
We called Adam by 21. He's 6-0 with a 59-7 all-play, which means nothing about this is luck. Noah is 1-5 and 11th in scoring, which historically is right where he likes to lurk.

copies.headline: Logan's Pittsburgh Flyers Bury Pukachu
copies.body:
The gap was everywhere but the margin came from the spots nobody drafts for. Germie Bernard put up 25.7 in Logan's flex against Brock Bowers' 11.0, Isaiah Likely went 23.9 on a John tight end room that got 12.3 from Trey McBride, and the Jaguars defense turned in minus-2.0 while the Chiefs banked 14.0. That's 42.3 from flex, tight end and defense alone, which is most of a 52.4-point win. Logan's kicker outscored John's by 8.6 for dessert.
John actually won the only position he was supposed to dominate — D'Andre Swift and Kyren Williams took the backfield by 10.5 — but the Rams connection failed him. Puka Nacua managed 14.0 on a 22.8 projection, Kyren came in at 9.7 on 21.0, Bowers at 11.0 on 19.8. Wan'Dale Robinson's 5.2 was the final insult.
We picked John by 16; that aged like milk. Logan's at 152.5, his season high, and the all-play says 2-4 was always fiction. John drops to 3-3 scoring second-best in the league. Both of these guys are better than their records.

copies.headline: Isaac Starts Two Zeroes, Loses By 45
copies.body:
The backfield ended this before noon. Christian got 39.6 from Bhayshul Tuten and Alvin Kamara; Isaac got 13.0 from Javonte Williams and then nothing at all, because Cam Skattebo and Saquon Barkley in the flex combined for a clean 0.0. Two empty roster spots is not a bad break, it's a lineup you have to answer for, especially with J.K. Dobbins (13.6) and Jakobi Meyers (13.3) sitting there. Add Jameis Winston posting 6.5 against an 17.8 projection while C.J. Stroud banked 23.0 on the bench and the quarterback gap alone was 13.7.
Christian wasn't clean either — Pat Freiermuth gave him 3.1 on an 11.1 projection, Brandon Aubrey kicked for a single point, and Trevor Lawrence's 27.3 rotted next to Jordan Love. Didn't matter. Love, DeVonta Smith and George Kittle all cleared 17 and the margin never got interesting.
We had Christian by 14; he covered it three times over. At 2-4 with 127.7 a game and a 39-27 all-play, he's the best bad record in the league. Isaac, 79.0 for a season low and dead last in every scoring metric, is 2-4 and has earned less than that.

copies.headline: Pitts and McCaffrey Outrun Grant's Special Teams
copies.body:
Leif won this at the two spots nobody drafts for: tight end and flex. Kyle Pitts put up 23.0 against Brenton Strange's 9.4, and Christian McCaffrey's 30.7 in the flex buried Dallas Goedert's 12.1. That's a 32-point swing in two lineup slots, which is the only reason Leif survived getting beaten at quarterback, running back, receiver, kicker and defense. Grant's Chris Boswell outscored Jason Myers by 10.0 and the Ravens D/ST beat the Texans' minus-2.0 by a full 12.0, and it still wasn't enough.
The misses were everywhere. Derrick Henry managed 5.0 on an 18.3 projection, Davante Adams 6.9 on 16.0, Josh Allen 18.3 on 25.1. Stefon Diggs scored 16.4 on Leif's bench while Adams did nothing. Grant had his own version — Keon Coleman 15.9 benched behind Christian Watson's 9.4, which is the entire 6.8-point margin and then some.
Leif is 4-2 with the 3rd-best scoring average and a 40-26 all-play; this one's earned. Grant falls to 3-3 at 39% all-play, still living on luck he hasn't repaid. We had Leif by 16 — close enough.

copies.headline: CJ's Backfield Buries Mitchell's Dead Flex
copies.body:
The running backs ended this one before noon. Jonathan Taylor and Chuba Hubbard combined for 40.2 while Mitchell got 17.5, and 15.7 of that was Rachaad White — Tyjae Spears managed 1.8 on an 8.7 projection, which is a stat line and not a performance. Add Tyler Shough's 27 against Dak Prescott's 11.0, plus eight points of kicker gap, and CJ had a 39.9-point win locked up without his tight end scoring a single point.
Mitchell's flex was a zero. DJ Moore did nothing while George Holani put up 8.0 on the bench, and the 85.5 total is his worst of the season. He's 1-5 with an all-play of 27-39 now, which means the bad luck story is running out of road — the scoring has come down to meet the record.
CJ wins his fourth, though Emeka Egbuka's 17.8 rotting behind Emanuel Wilson suggests he's not exactly optimizing. We had him by 11; he took it by 40. The human coin flip has landed tails five times.

copies.headline: Peter's Receivers Vanish, Kaleb Walks Away
copies.body:
The wideouts decided this one and it wasn't close: Kaleb got 31.2 from Drake London and Carnell Tate's 19.0 breakout, Peter got 15.8 total and most of that was George Pickens doing it alone. Add the running backs — Ashton Jeanty 15.8 and RJ Harvey 14.6 against Bijan Robinson's 7.3 — and Kaleb had the thing banked before the kickers mattered. Bijan was projected for 23.0. He produced less than Dameon Pierce. That's how you post 69.8, a season low by 25-plus.
Peter's misses compounded: Denzel Boston 2.5 on a 13.5 projection with Romeo Doubs and his 11.2 sitting right there, A.J. Brown 5.7 on 12.7. We picked Peter by 13, which looks worse every time you reread the box score. Kaleb didn't earn this cleanly either — Tre Tucker put up 26.7 on his bench while Ladd McConkey managed 2.7 — but 94.4 was plenty.
Both sit 4-2 with all-plays in the 40s and 30s, meaning the 2022 champ and the 2023 champ are each running about a win and a half ahead of their actual football. Someone has to pay that back.

intro: Leif-Grant was the only game that required any sweating, a 6.8-point margin that stood alone on a slate where four of six teams won by 24 or more. Logan's 152.5 was the week's ceiling and John's 100.1 couldn't get within 50 of it, while Christian needed nothing special to bury Isaac's 78.98. Peter put up 69.78 and still had the decency to show up Monday morning.
